Albanese theorems consume (SymPowColimit.hasColimit_permDiagram_iff), so the reduction is
lossless. Over.forget creates colimits, so no over-category bookkeeping is needed: it is a
statement about Scheme.

.lean (the S_n-action on the n-fold tensor power of a RING -- mathlib had permutation only as
a linear equiv, so Milne's carrier was not even STATEABLE) and SymPowInvariantsUnder.lean
(the invariants ARE the limit in Under k, dually a colimit in (Under k)^op).

subproject. One of the three closed this round: StableAffineCoverGroup.lean proves every
point has a G-STABLE affine open neighbourhood for a bare finite group -- the same proof as
Picard/StableAffineCover.lean, whose Galois binder its body never touches. The other two:
(i) cocycle/overlap agreement of the affine chart quotients; (ii) OrbitsInAffineOpen for the
curve, which is where quasi-projectivity enters and mathlib has no quasi-projectivity
vocabulary at this pin.

bill is DONE (Albanese/TensorPowerCofan.lean packages the tensor power as the n-ary coproduct

ID: AJC.albanese.universal | status: active | owner: ajc-albanese | milestone: 
TITLE: Albanese universal property
SUMMARY:
Albanese universal property. THE ARGUMENT IS PROVED (run 0069); what remains is one precisely-named typeclass instance, not "one missing object" in general.

MILNE III.6.1 IS PROVED, both connector directions, over the symmetric power taken as an interface rather than a sorry -- Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean and Albanese/AlbaneseJacobian.lean, sorry-free. Forward (symAVMap_eq_of_albanese_eq) needs psi to be a HOMOMORPHISM: pushing psi through the g-fold sum is map_prod (IsMonHom.monoidHom), exactly where Milne's step 5 uses homomorphy. Backward (albanese_eq_of_symAVMap_eq) needs neither that nor the quotient universal property -- it is restriction along Q |-> (Q,P0,...,P0) plus the collapse basePointShift_comp_powSum.

THE RESIDUE IS NOW PRECISE (Albanese/AlbaneseFromColimit.lean, corrected 2026-07-28 commit af3d7b6a2 after an earlier draft got the binder wrong): exists_unique_albanese_of_scheme_colimits takes no SymPowData argument and no hproj argument -- the symmetric power is symPowOfColimit C g and its symmetry is colimit.w, free at every n. The single remaining typeclass hypothesis is HasColimit (permDiagram C g): ONE diagram, for THIS curve and THIS g, in Over (Spec kbar). It is NOT HasColimitsOfShape (SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin g))) Scheme -- that shape-quantified form is strictly stronger, is not what hasColimit_permDiagram_iff covers, and is believed FALSE at this pin (schemes have no coequalizers in general); a theorem carrying it would be vacuous. See AJC.albanese.symmetric for the state of discharging that instance. UPDATED run 0069 r7: this row previously said "TWO residues now, in order: the Cofan/IsColimit packaging in (Under k)-op ... and then the gluing". The FIRST is closed (Albanese/TensorPowerCofan.lean), so there is ONE residue left and it is the geometric wall: the gluing/cocycle compatibility of the chart quotients plus OrbitsInAffineOpen for the curve, where quasi-projectivity enters and mathlib has no such vocabulary at this pin. r7 also named the affine carrier at both ends (SymPowAffineCarrier.tensorPowerOpIsoPiObj for the input, SymPowAffineQuotient.colimitPermDiagramIsoFixed for the quotient = Milne III.3 Prop 3.1's affine half with the object identified), which discharged SymPowColimit §5's "carrier is not named in Lean" caveat. NONE of that shortens the curve residue: the affine chain is stated over mkUnder k A in (Under k)-op, and C is a proper curve in Over (Spec kbar). Do not read "3 of 4 items supplied" as "3/4 of the way to Sym^g C" -- item 4 is the whole of the geometry.

THE MEASUREMENT, which attributes the residual sorry rather than asserting whose it is:
    #print axioms exists_unique_albanese_of_scheme_colimits -> [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]  AXIOM-CLEAN
    #print axioms Pic0.albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData    -> [propext, sorryAx, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
Same statement; the sole difference is whether the target group object is Pic0.jacobianScheme C or an arbitrary abelian variety. So the entire sorryAx residue of the Pic0 form is the PICARD REPRESENTABILITY SEAM upstream of this leg, and none of it is Milne's argument.

DISCHARGED UNCONDITIONALLY (Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean, on the project's four-instance abelian-variety package): commutativity of an abelian variety (Milne I.1.4) and pointed rigidity (Milne I.1.2). The obstruction had been instance KEYING through the monoidal notation, not missing mathematics.

REMAINING INPUTS: (1) HasColimit (permDiagram C g) -- see AJC.albanese.symmetric; (2) Milne III.5.1(a) birationality as a SECTION of f^(g) over a dense open. The descent around them is closed: extend_to_av (Milne Thm 3.2) is unconditional and axiom-clean, and exists_unique_descent_of_section / hom_ext_of_dense_open package it in elementary terms with no rational map in the statement.

NOT A CLOSED RESULT ABOUT THE JACOBIAN, and the module headers say so in those words. The pinned Pic0.albanese_universal_property still reports sorryAx and its six sorries in AlbaneseUP.lean are UNCHANGED -- they are stated against a sorry-BODIED SymmetricPower and are undischargeable as stated, which the AlbaneseUP.lean header now records along with a pointer to where the mathematics lives.

11:# The `G`-stable affine cover for a bare finite group action
12:
13:`Sym^n C` is a quotient of `C^n` by `S_n`, and the route to it that
14:`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` §6 identifies — explicit `Scheme.GlueData` from affine charts —
15:needs one geometric input above all others: **every point has an affine open neighbourhood
16:stable under the whole group**. Without it the charts cannot be chosen compatibly and the
17:quotient exists only as an algebraic space (the Hironaka trap recorded in
18:`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`).
19:
20:That input was believed missing for `S_n`. It is not: `Picard/StableAffineCover.lean` proves
21:it, sorry-free, and its proof **never uses the Galois structure it is stated over**.
22:
23:## What was actually going on
24:
25:`Picard/StableAffineCover.lean`'s `exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbitsInAffineOpen` is stated
26:for a `SemilinearGalAction K L X f` — a group homomorphism `Gal(L/K) →* Aut X` *together with*
27:a field `compat`, the commuting square over `Spec γ` that makes the action semilinear. Reading
28:the proof, the only things it consumes are `ρ.act` and the two one-line consequences
29:`act_one_hom` / `act_mul_hom`, which are `map_one` and `map_mul` of the underlying
30:`MonoidHom`. `compat` — all of the semilinearity — is never mentioned, and
31:`[FiniteDimensional K L]` is spent only on getting a `Fintype` for `Finset.univ`.
32:
33:So the theorem is about a **finite group acting on a scheme by automorphisms**; the Galois
34:data decorates the statement. This file states that version. It is a re-derivation, not a
35:generalisation of the original in place: `Picard/` belongs to another lane, so the proof is
36:copied here with the binder replaced (`G →* Aut X` plus `Fintype G`) rather than the original
37:being weakened. The two files should eventually be one, and the note below says which
38:direction that should go.
39:
40:## Main results
41:
42:* `StableGroupAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` — the EGA II 4.5.4 hypothesis, for a bare action:
43:  every orbit lies in an affine open. Essential, not technical — see the Hironaka trap.
44:* `StableGroupAction.IsStableOpen` — a `G`-stable open.
45:* `exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbits` — **the theorem**: under that hypothesis every point
46:  has a `G`-stable affine open neighbourhood. Prime avoidance puts the orbit in a basic open
47:  `D(s)` inside `⋂_g g⁻¹U`, and the norm `N = ∏_g g(s)` cuts out a stable affine basic open.
48:* `exists_stable_affineOpen_perm` — **the `S_n` instantiation**: for `C` a `k̄`-scheme, every
49:  point of `C^n` has an `S_n`-stable affine open neighbourhood, given the orbit hypothesis.
50:
51:**Correction (2026-07-29): the `S_n` producer exists and this file's scope note said it did
52:not.** Two earlier revisions ran in opposite directions and both were wrong. One advertised a
53:`permAction : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) →* Aut (C^n)` that did not exist; the correction then
54:recorded building it as blocked, on the grounds that `MonObj.permAut` "is a bare morphism
55:never shown to be an isomorphism" and `SymPowColimit.permEnd` "lands in `End`, not `Aut`".
56:Both grounds were accurate statements about the tree and the inference from them was not:
57:`permAut C σ⁻¹` is a two-sided inverse of `permAut C σ`, because
58:`permAut C σ ≫ permAut C τ = permAut C (σ * τ)`. That is `MonObj.permAut_comp`, and the
59:action is `MonObj.permAutHom`, both now in `Albanese/GrpObjFoldSum.lean` — four lines, no
60:construction. The lesson is the `permEnd` convention: the inverse `permEnd` carries is forced
61:by `End`'s reversed multiplication, and reading it as a fact about `permAut` is what made an
62:isomorphism look absent.
63:
64:## Why the proof needs no averaging, and so no characteristic hypothesis
65:
66:The norm `∏_g g(s)` is a *product*, not an average: it needs no `1/|G|` and works in every
67:characteristic. That matters here for the same reason it matters in
68:`Albanese/SymPowTensorAction.lean` — `g!` may vanish in `k̄` when `char k̄ ≤ g`, so any route
69:through averaging would exclude exactly the cases the challenge is stated over.
70:
71:## Scope — what this does and does not give
72:
73:**Does**: prove the stable-cover statement at the generality a glue-data construction wants —
74:a *finite group acting on a scheme by automorphisms*, with no Galois hypothesis and no
75:characteristic hypothesis.
76:
77:**Does** now also apply it to `S_n` acting on `C^n`: `exists_stable_affineOpen_perm` for the
78:product in `Scheme`, and `exists_stable_affineOpen_perm_over` for the underlying scheme of the
79:`Over (Spec k̄)`-product — **which is the one the leg uses**, and is a different object (see
80:that theorem's docstring; `Over.forget` does not preserve binary products).
81:
82:**Does not**: build the glue data. `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)` remains open and
83:`AlbaneseUP.lean`'s six sorries are unchanged.
84:
85:**The count, in one place, because three places in this tree disagreed about it.** A glue-data
86:assembly needs *four* things:
87:
88:1. ✓ a `G`-stable affine cover — below, with both `S_n` instantiations.
89:2. ✓ the `Aut`-valued `S_n`-action — `MonObj.permAutHom` (`Albanese/GrpObjFoldSum.lean`).
90:3. ✓ **(completed run 0069 r7; this entry read "Partly" until then.)** The `n`-ary coproduct of
91:   commutative algebras = `n`-fold tensor power, with the permutation action matched to

93:   (`existsUnique_coprodLift`, `coprodLift_permAlgHom`, `permAlgHom_comp_singleAlgHom`); the

11:# The `G`-stable affine cover for a bare finite group action
12:
13:`Sym^n C` is a quotient of `C^n` by `S_n`, and the route to it that
14:`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` §6 identifies — explicit `Scheme.GlueData` from affine charts —
15:needs one geometric input above all others: **every point has an affine open neighbourhood
16:stable under the whole group**. Without it the charts cannot be chosen compatibly and the
17:quotient exists only as an algebraic space (the Hironaka trap recorded in
18:`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`).
19:
20:That input was believed missing for `S_n`. It is not: `Picard/StableAffineCover.lean` proves
21:it, sorry-free, and its proof **never uses the Galois structure it is stated over**.
22:
23:## What was actually going on
24:
25:`Picard/StableAffineCover.lean`'s `exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbitsInAffineOpen` is stated
26:for a `SemilinearGalAction K L X f` — a group homomorphism `Gal(L/K) →* Aut X` *together with*
27:a field `compat`, the commuting square over `Spec γ` that makes the action semilinear. Reading
28:the proof, the only things it consumes are `ρ.act` and the two one-line consequences
29:`act_one_hom` / `act_mul_hom`, which are `map_one` and `map_mul` of the underlying
30:`MonoidHom`. `compat` — all of the semilinearity — is never mentioned, and
31:`[FiniteDimensional K L]` is spent only on getting a `Fintype` for `Finset.univ`.
32:
33:So the theorem is about a **finite group acting on a scheme by automorphisms**; the Galois
34:data decorates the statement. This file states that version. It is a re-derivation, not a
35:generalisation of the original in place: `Picard/` belongs to another lane, so the proof is
36:copied here with the binder replaced (`G →* Aut X` plus `Fintype G`) rather than the original
37:being weakened. The two files should eventually be one, and the note below says which
38:direction that should go.
39:
40:## Main results
41:
42:* `StableGroupAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` — the EGA II 4.5.4 hypothesis, for a bare action:
43:  every orbit lies in an affine open. Essential, not technical — see the Hironaka trap.
44:* `StableGroupAction.IsStableOpen` — a `G`-stable open.
45:* `exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbits` — **the theorem**: under that hypothesis every point
46:  has a `G`-stable affine open neighbourhood. Prime avoidance puts the orbit in a basic open
47:  `D(s)` inside `⋂_g g⁻¹U`, and the norm `N = ∏_g g(s)` cuts out a stable affine basic open.
48:* `exists_stable_affineOpen_perm` — **the `S_n` instantiation**: for `C` a `k̄`-scheme, every
49:  point of `C^n` has an `S_n`-stable affine open neighbourhood, given the orbit hypothesis.
50:
51:**Correction (2026-07-29): the `S_n` producer exists and this file's scope note said it did
52:not.** Two earlier revisions ran in opposite directions and both were wrong. One advertised a
53:`permAction : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) →* Aut (C^n)` that did not exist; the correction then
54:recorded building it as blocked, on the grounds that `MonObj.permAut` "is a bare morphism
55:never shown to be an isomorphism" and `SymPowColimit.permEnd` "lands in `End`, not `Aut`".
56:Both grounds were accurate statements about the tree and the inference from them was not:
57:`permAut C σ⁻¹` is a two-sided inverse of `permAut C σ`, because
58:`permAut C σ ≫ permAut C τ = permAut C (σ * τ)`. That is `MonObj.permAut_comp`, and the
59:action is `MonObj.permAutHom`, both now in `Albanese/GrpObjFoldSum.lean` — four lines, no
60:construction. The lesson is the `permEnd` convention: the inverse `permEnd` carries is forced
61:by `End`'s reversed multiplication, and reading it as a fact about `permAut` is what made an
62:isomorphism look absent.
63:
64:## Why the proof needs no averaging, and so no characteristic hypothesis
65:
66:The norm `∏_g g(s)` is a *product*, not an average: it needs no `1/|G|` and works in every
67:characteristic. That matters here for the same reason it matters in
68:`Albanese/SymPowTensorAction.lean` — `g!` may vanish in `k̄` when `char k̄ ≤ g`, so any route
69:through averaging would exclude exactly the cases the challenge is stated over.
70:

72:
73:**Does**: prove the stable-cover statement at the generality a glue-data construction wants —
74:a *finite group acting on a scheme by automorphisms*, with no Galois hypothesis and no
75:characteristic hypothesis.
76:
77:**Does** now also apply it to `S_n` acting on `C^n`: `exists_stable_affineOpen_perm` for the
78:product in `Scheme`, and `exists_stable_affineOpen_perm_over` for the underlying scheme of the
79:`Over (Spec k̄)`-product — **which is the one the leg uses**, and is a different object (see
80:that theorem's docstring; `Over.forget` does not preserve binary products).
81:
82:**Does not**: build the glue data. `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)` remains open and
83:`AlbaneseUP.lean`'s six sorries are unchanged.

89:2. ✓ the `Aut`-valued `S_n`-action — `MonObj.permAutHom` (`Albanese/GrpObjFoldSum.lean`).

name: hgraph
description: The dependency graph — Horizon's vendored hgraph core keeps one file per statement/Lean declaration under <project>/hgraph/; `horizon graph frontier` ranks work and agents attach node-scoped comments and reviews. This is the only DAG engine.
---

Each project may carry an **hgraph**: a plain-files semantic graph under
`<project>/hgraph/` — one Markdown node per blueprint statement and per Lean
declaration, typed edges (`uses` = the hard dependency DAG, `formalizes` =
informal↔formal identity). `horizon graph sync` (run automatically at run boundaries)
reconciles the blueprint + Lean sources into it; your **authored** additions
(comments, reviews, metadata) are never touched by sync. The files are
committed to the workspace ledger like everything else.

Use `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …`; when a workspace has one project,
`-p` is optional. Address nodes by `label:<latex-label>` or
`decl:<lean-fqname>` — raw ids are opaque hashes. Most commands accept `--json`.

## Sync it yourself — and act on the warnings

Don't wait for the run boundary: after you change blueprint statements,
`\uses{}`/`\lean{}` annotations, or Lean declarations, run
`"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> sync` and **read its output**. Sync prints warnings for exactly the defects
you can fix on the spot: `\uses{X} has no blueprint node` (missing/mistyped
label), `\lean{Name} not found in Lean sources` (renamed or unwritten
declaration), stale nodes whose source vanished. Fix what your change caused
before moving on; a warning you deliberately leave (e.g. a forward reference
you'll write next) gets a node comment or a memory item so the next session
knows it's intentional. Sync is idempotent and never touches your authored
comments/reviews/metadata.

## Read

- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> list --state ready` — nodes whose dependencies are all closed:
  provable *now*. Other states: `closed`, `blocked`, `formalized_open`.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` — the ready nodes ranked by how many downstream nodes a
  proof would unlock. **Use this when picking the next node to prove.**
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:thm:foo` — one node: statement, `lean_status`
  (`lean_ok | mathlib_ok | sorry | empty`, derived from scanning the Lean, not
  from `\leanok`), deps, attached comments/reviews.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> ancestors label:thm:foo` — the dependency cone.
